experiments.hypothesis: Unused AES inverse-key setup, ciphertext staging and scanning beyond an ordered option add avoidable work.
experiments.change: Core #651 uses the encryption-only AES type, separate-input CCM opening and early option-iterator exhaustion. No App, pool or security-context fields added.
experiments.result: The combined batch changes median window mean poll wall time by about 3% unprotected and 1.5% OSCORE. This does not isolate the contribution of each change or establish process CPU improvement.
experiments.decision: Merged after focused library, feature and independent reviews; continue profiling.

experiments.hypothesis: Repeated nonblocking receive attempts consume CPU while no request is available.
experiments.change: Give the Mio and ready host fixtures equivalent OSCORE configuration and wait for App deadlines rather than a fixed millisecond tick.
experiments.result: At 2000 scheduled 64-byte operations/s, readiness reduces median server process CPU by about 95% unprotected and 97% OSCORE, with roughly 12 microseconds additional median RTT. CPU windows were successive batches and accounting is quantized.
experiments.decision: Retain the adapter support and all observations. The latency tradeoff and narrow workload leave acceptance unfinished.

experiments.hypothesis: CPU and scheduling stacks can distinguish core work from transport and idle-poll costs.
experiments.change: A symbolized release server ran under a fixed 32 MiB circular WPR CPU/scheduling profile with 30000 verified 64-byte operations at 6000/s.
experiments.result: The private trace saved and Rust symbols resolve, but the circular buffer retained sampled CPU only from 5.386528 to 7.732580 seconds of a 7.732580-second trace. Zero lost-event counters do not establish workload coverage. Instrumented process CPU is not a clean comparison.
experiments.evidence: Private trace, frequency report, raw native diagnostic and pinned build manifest retained outside this repository.
experiments.decision: Reject whole-window attribution from this capture. Stage a sampled-only 64 MiB profile; further Windows elevation is deferred by the operator.

experiments.hypothesis: Rotated matched-load CPU windows and separate perf captures will resolve active processing and syscall costs more clearly.
experiments.change: Manual Linux runner uses immutable revisions, a frozen baseline client, sequential builds, complete authenticated operations and bounded artifacts.
experiments.result: Run39779276076 completed 24 clean windows and 24 separate profiles: 1,872,000 verified operations, zero failures. At64B,C1,6000/s, both builds actually used matched Rust1.99.1. Same-adapter candidate/baseline CPU ratios range0.9535..1.0877; no50%target proof. All52 Linux tests passed. Most kernel samples unresolved; readiness captures27..53 samples and zero duration headers do not prove coverage.
experiments.decision: Retain all results and warnings. Investigate repeated receive/poll maintenance; enforce selected compiler before future builds. Do not treat cross-adapter savings as core speedup.
